name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse (POP-Q Staging) and Female Urinary Incontinence

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / ICS Guidelines on Urogynecology
clinicalPearls: POP-Q system standardizes prolapse quantification using six anatomical points measured relative to the hymeneal ring
Stage III prolapse extends more than one centimeter beyond the hymen but less than total vaginal length minus two centimeters
Stress urinary incontinence is involuntary leakage on effort due to urethral hypermobility or intrinsic sphincter deficiency
Mid-urethral synthetic mesh slings (TVT / TOT) provide gold-standard surgical cure for stress urinary incontinence
Urgency urinary incontinence is detrusor overactivity treated first-line with bladder training and antimuscarinics or mirabegron
reference.pathophysiology: Pelvic organ support depends on Level I apical suspension (cardinal/uterosacral ligaments), Level II lateral attachment (arcus tendineus fasciae pelvis), and Level III distal perineal anchoring. Childbirth trauma, chronic intra-abdominal pressure, and postmenopausal estrogen loss lead to levator ani avulsion and endopelvic fascial attenuation. Incontinence stems from loss of bladder neck support or non-inhibited detrusor smooth muscle contractions.
additionalDifferentials: Stress incontinence versus urgency incontinence versus overflow incontinence
additionalInvestigations: POP-Q standardized examination in dorsal lithotomy under maximal Valsalva
Multichannel urodynamic studies (cystometry and leak point pressure)
Post-void residual urine volume measurement via catheterization or ultrasound
